clinics.name: Hospital Galenia
clinics.district: Cancún (Supermanzana 12, Av. Tulum at Nizuc)
clinics.namedDoctors: The site has a doctor directory with individual profiles; some list English as a spoken language. No surgeons or anesthesiologists are named on the medical-tourism page itself. Surgery takes place in the hospital's own operating rooms (quirófanos) with adult, pediatric and neonatal ICUs on site.
clinics.credentials: CSG: the hospital displays the Consejo de Salubridad General 'Certificación de Establecimientos de Atención Médica' seal on its medical-tourism page; the CSG certified-establishment list at csg.gob.mx could not be opened on October 30, 2026 (page returned 404 or blank), so validity dates are unverified. JCI: claimed on the hospital site; the JCI directory blocked automated reading (HTTP 403) on October 30, 2026, so the claim is as stated by the hospital. Also claims Accreditation Canada International and the SECTUR 'Distintivo Turismo de Salud'. Member of Consorcio Mexicano de Hospitales and Asociación Nacional de Hospitales Privados (hospital site). Cash-pay patients can request complication insurance through a Novamar Insurance arrangement and financing through United Medical Credit (hospital site). Year founded not stated on the site.
clinics.cautions: In August 2022 COFEPRIS closed the hospital's blood bank, saying it was operating without a sanitary licence and taking blood samples without meeting health criteria; the press report did not say whether it later reopened (galenia-press-poresto). No deaths, lawsuits or US agency notices naming the hospital were found in press searches.
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site. The medical-tourism page states procedures are paid out of pocket and lists insurers it bills (AXA, GNP, MetLife, Allianz, BUPA, AXA Assistance).

booking.channels: Medical tourism office (Dirección Comercial y Turismo Médico): phone +52 998 891 5200 ext. 632; email medicaltourism@hospitalgalenia.com; general line +52 998 891 5200 and info@hospitalgalenia.com; contact form on the medical-tourism page. No WhatsApp listed. Hours not stated.
booking.consult: Not published. The page offers only the form, phone and email. An estimate is requested by describing the procedure to the medical-tourism office; no document list or response time is stated.
booking.languages: Spanish and English site; individual doctors list English.

Hospiten is a Spanish hospital group (Tenerife) that bought three Amerimed hospitals in Puerto Vallarta, San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas in November 2014 (hospiten-amerimed-alimarket). clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site. An imaging campaign mentions preferential rates without figures. An online payment portal is linked.

booking.consult: Not published. For insured patients the site asks for ID, insurance card, prior authorization and medical reports; cash-pay estimate process is not described. The group's services page says an interpreting service is available in several languages.
booking.languages: Spanish and English site; interpreting service stated at group level.

clinics.name: Hospital Amerimed Cancún
clinics.district: Cancún (Av. Tulum Sur 260, Supermanzana 7, Centro)
clinics.namedDoctors: Not named on the hospital site. The site says staff are bilingual and the hospital operates 24 hours. Surgery takes place in the hospital.
clinics.credentials: CSG: no certification is claimed on the hospital site; the CSG list at csg.gob.mx could not be opened on October 30, 2026. JCI: not claimed on the site (a third-party directory shows JCI for Amerimed Cozumel, not Cancún; unverified). The site footer is dated 2021 and the hospital has no stated international-patient department. Amerimed sold its Pacific-coast hospitals to Hospiten in 2014 (hospiten-amerimed-alimarket); the Cancún hospital still operates under the Amerimed name. Year founded not stated on the site (a 2016 US news report said the chain was founded in 1996).
clinics.cautions: In August 2016, Becker's Hospital Review, citing the Indianapolis Star, reported that the family of an Indiana tourist treated at Amerimed Cancún for blocked arteries said the hospital would not release her until most of a bill of about $53,000 was paid; a lawyer for the hospital said it never refuses to release a non-paying patient for financial reasons, and the US Consulate in Mérida said a hospital cannot legally stop a patient leaving over an unpaid bill (amerimed-press-beckers). Local Indianapolis coverage put the total demanded at about $111,000 and said the family still owed about $35,000 after leaving (amerimed-press-wrtv). Structural caveat for any Cancún emergency admission: US insurance and Medicaid are generally not accepted and large upfront payments were demanded in this case.
clinics.publishedPrices: Maternity packages shown on the site as $21,000 for cesarean and $28,000 for vaginal delivery with the currency shown only as '$' (presumably MXN; not converted). No other prices published.

booking.channels: Phone +52 998 881 3400; email contacto@amerimedhospitals.com; no WhatsApp or international-patient line listed. Hours: hospital open 24/7.
booking.consult: Not published. The site has an insurers section but no estimate process for foreign cash-pay patients.
booking.languages: Bilingual staff stated (Spanish and English).

clinics.name: GIOSTAR Mexico (Global Institute of Stem Cell Therapy and Research)
clinics.district: Playa del Carmen (Av. 10 Lote 1 Local 46, Playacar) with stated clinics in Cancún and Los Algodones
clinics.namedDoctors: Dr. Anand Srivastava, PhD (co-founder and chairman, San Diego; not a physician); Dr. Cristina Santana, MD (medical director, Playa del Carmen, UNAM); Dr. Daniel Garza and Dr. Evelyn García (regenerative and aesthetic medicine) per the Mexico site and marketplace listings. No cédula numbers shown. Treatments are given in the clinic's own premises, not a hospital; CSG certification does not apply.
clinics.credentials: COFEPRIS: the Mexico site says its clinics are COFEPRIS-licensed but shows no numbers; a marketplace listing shows licence numbers 19-TR-23-008-0002 (described as stem cell bank) and 19-TR-23-008-0001 (stem cell transplant) for Playa del Carmen, and Bookimed shows licence images dated 2019 and 2024; none were verified against COFEPRIS's registry, which was not fetchable, and the Bookimed page also displays 2019 licences issued to a different company (Sani Dental Group). COFEPRIS permits the handling of cells under a licence for cell banks and transplant establishments; a licence to operate does not mean a therapy is proven. These therapies are not approved by the US FDA for the conditions marketed. No COFEPRIS alert or suspension naming GIOSTAR was found. The company's US headquarters is in San Diego.
clinics.cautions: A California patient sued the US entity in 2020 (Mendez v. Global Institute of Stem Cell Therapy and Research USA et al.), alleging stem cell treatment given to a cancer patient without proper cell matching; outcome not confirmed. Los Angeles Times columnist Michael Hiltzik reported that the company acknowledged exaggerating a co-founder's academic appointments and that two listed advisers denied any connection, and questioned its clinical-trial claims; a stem cell scientist's blog summarizing this found no ClinicalTrials.gov listings for GIOSTAR (giostar-ipscell). Marketplace listings mark the Mexico clinic as 'not accepting new requests'. The Mexico site contains no FDA or efficacy disclaimer. Structural caveat: outpatient clinic in a retail plaza; no ICU or hospital backup described.
clinics.publishedPrices: Not published on its site (cost blog linked without figures). Marketplace range (indicative), Bookimed, last updated March 29, 2025: neuropathy $14,870 USD; multiple sclerosis $17,000; autism $8,000 to $15,600; cerebral palsy $15,000 to $24,000.
